themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis This Week
themes_detail.summary: Street conditions in Central Harlem have spiked dramatically this week with 37 complaints filed versus a baseline of 4.6 per week—a 700% increase (z-score: 15.73)—signaling a sudden, acute deterioration in road surfaces that demands immediate investigation into cause and scope.
evidence: 37 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike)
Z-score of 15.73 indicates statistically extreme deviation from baseline
411 building permits filed in last 90 days (348 alterations + 26 alteration COs) suggests possible infrastructure work or structural damage
reporting_angles: Ground truth: Visit neighborhoods with highest concentration of complaints to document street conditions and interview affected residents/business owners
DOB/DOT angle: File FOIL request for street work orders, emergency repairs, and infrastructure projects filed this week in CD 110

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk & Street Noise Degradation
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, street and sidewalk conditions have deteriorated sharply: street/sidewalk noise jumped 287% (160 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 41.4 weekly average) and sidewalk condition complaints rose 106% (8 vs. 3.9 average), suggesting environmental or human-activity changes affecting pedestrian experience.
evidence: Noise - Street/Sidewalk: 160 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 41.4 weekly average (287% spike, z-score: 10.44)
Sidewalk Condition complaints: 8 (2 weeks ago) vs. 3.9 average (106% spike, z-score: 5.28)
Noise - Vehicle complaints also up 220% (16 vs. 5.0 average 2 weeks ago, z-score: 5.34)
reporting_angles: Temporal mapping: Identify which neighborhoods/corridors (125th St, Broadway, etc.) account for concentrated complaints; interview residents about patterns (time of day, source)
Root cause analysis: Check for street events, construction, traffic diversions, or enforcement changes that coincide with spike 2 weeks ago

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Acceleration
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints in Central Harlem jumped 105% last week (33 complaints vs. 16.1 weekly average, z-score: 5.59), marking a statistically significant spike that may indicate spreading infestation, seasonal surge, or deteriorating sanitation conditions requiring urgent public health attention.
evidence: 33 rodent complaints LAST WEEK vs. 16.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (105% spike, z-score: 5.59)
Unsanitary Condition complaints remain elevated at 1,306 over 90 days (potential contributing factor)
Litter Basket Complaints also spiked 700% last week (3 vs. 0.4 average, z-score: 5.42), suggesting food/waste accumulation
reporting_angles: Public health angle: Contact NYC Health + Hospitals and DOHMH to determine if rodent complaints are tied to known infestation areas, what interventions are underway
Resident impact: Interview families in buildings with recent complaints about health effects, displacement, landlord response

themes_detail.label: Vendor & Commercial Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor Enforcement and Commercial Disposal complaints have both spiked 2,300% (3 complaints each vs. baseline of 0.1 weekly average, z-score: 8.69) 2–3 weeks ago, suggesting either a sudden change in illegal street vending, food vendor operations, or enforcement activity that warrants clarification.
evidence: Vendor Enforcement complaints: 3 (2 weeks ago) vs. 0.1 weekly average (2,300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Commercial Disposal Complaint: 3 (3 weeks ago) vs. 0.1 weekly average (2,300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Baseline is extremely low, making even small absolute numbers statistically anomalous
reporting_angles: Enforcement angle: Check with NYPD, DOE (Sanitation), and HCA (Department of Consumer Affairs) for changes in street vendor or food cart enforcement operations in Harlem 2–3 weeks ago
Street economy impact: Interview vendors and nearby business owners about whether enforcement has increased or commercial waste collection has changed

themes_detail.label: Long-Standing Homelessness & Facilities Gap
themes_detail.summary: Community Board budget requests reveal a persistent, unfunded need to upgrade homeless services facilities—the same request reappears year after year—suggesting a structural service gap that may contribute to visible street conditions and sanitation complaints throughout the district.
evidence: Community Board budget request (recurring, unfunded): 'Upgrade existing facilities for the homeless' (DHS)
Appears year-after-year in budget cycle, indicating chronic underfunding
Correlates with elevated unsanitary condition complaints (1,306 over 90 days) and street condition deterioration
reporting_angles: Systems investigation: Interview CB leadership about why this request goes unfunded; contact DHS for capacity, facility condition audit
Human impact: Profile residents and advocacy groups addressing homelessness in Harlem; document conditions at shelters and street encampments
